quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If you drink one drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Any amount of alcohol makes it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: Wearing what reduces your risk of serious injury in a motorcycle crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you wear to be more visible to other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Brightly-colored clothing makes other drivers see you more easily, day or night.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to leave your lane or go off the road.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue during a long ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may make you dangerously tired later when it wears off. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect against wind, rain, and snow on long rides.

questions.question: When scanning the road around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Look for potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: While looking for hazards, focus on finding escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the risk of taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can impair your ability to ride safely. Always ask your doctor how a new medication might affect your driving or riding.

questions.question: What should you do with gears when slowing or stopping a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the rider.
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the rider. Hold firmly onto the rider's waist, hips, or midsection. If the motorcycle has handgrips, you can hold onto those instead. Never sit sideways on a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is different about how alcohol enters your bloodstream?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Unlike other substances, alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream. It reaches the brain very quickly.

questions.question: When stopping with a passenger, what should you do differently?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier when you have a passenger. Also, reduce your speed and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: What can improve your chances of surviving a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-approved helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that is properly secured is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what happens if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Limit how many hours you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how many hours you ride each day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest during long trips, even if you are not tired. Most experienced riders do not ride more than six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain cause fatigue quickly, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Do not look ahead for hazards.
Do not use turn signals because they distract other drivers.
Make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, be visible to others, clearly signal your intentions, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, watch the road ahead, and identify hazards. Always be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: How do you achieve the best straight-line braking?

options.text: Use both brakes fully without locking either wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes fully without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Best braking is achieved by fully applying both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.

questions.question: What can reduce your chances of a collision?

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not your surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and reduces collision risk. Always be aware of other drivers so you can prepare for their movements.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly colored clothing to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective materials on your clothing also help make you visible.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space possible. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best foot protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: Make sure your brake lights work
Make sure the paint is not peeling
Make sure your bike is completely clean

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your brake lights work
questions.explanation: Always do safety checks before riding. Test both your front and rear brakes to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose so it flaps in the wind

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug so they don't flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane
You will get through the turn faster

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can make you cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning or entering a curve.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes with controlled pressure at the same time.

questions.question: How should you load saddlebags?

options.text: Load them as evenly as possible
Put as much weight as possible in one bag

questions.correctAnswerText: Load them as evenly as possible
questions.explanation: Put about the same weight in each saddlebag. Uneven weight can make your motorcycle drift to one side.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red
The light is about to turn green
Stop and wait for traffic to pass

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, what is important?

options.text: It should fit loosely and flap in the wind
It should fit snugly and not flap in the wind
It should not be made of leather or sturdy material

questions.correctAnswerText: It should fit snugly and not flap in the wind
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.
